title: Slotized KV cache sizing experiment - Jan 2025
content:
Purpose:
Quick experiment sheet exploring a slotized KV-cache allocation approach (per-tenant slots) instead of monolithic byte-capacity. Goal is to understand hit-rate sensitivity, cost impact, and operational knobs for bursty, multi-tenant workloads. This is a working notebook — many heuristics here are WIP.

Background / motivation:
- Current per-route prefix/KV caching uses a single pool with LRU eviction. That works but leads to noisy- neighbor eviction under multi-tenant burst patterns.
- Slotized allocation: partition cache into N fixed-size slots; each slot can be pinned to a tenant or route group for short windows, reducing cross-tenant churn and improving effective hit-rates for heavy hitters.
- Want to quantify: at what slot counts / slot sizes do we see net $ savings vs baseline? How does cold-eviction cost (recompute prefix tokens) affect ROI?

Assumptions (simplified for the model):
- Baseline: shared KV pool = 500 GB, global hit-rate baseline 18%, average request uses 120 warm tokens when hit, 0 when miss (miss means full forward).
- Token inference cost (GPU-run): $0.0000007 per token (raw execution cost; excludes infra amortization).
- Baseline effective tokens per request: 1024 tokens generated on average.
- Prefetch/probe overhead when slot pinned: 1.15x token usage for pinned warmups (some double-work during slot rotations).
- Traffic profile modeled as: 70% long-tail light users (median seq len 256), 30% heavy tenants (median seq len 800). Heavy tenants responsible for 60% of requests.
- Eviction pain: when a slot is reallocated, the first 5 requests incur cold cost of 300 tokens on average (probe+repopulate).

Experiment variables (columns simulated below):
- slots_total: number of slots in pool (e.g., 10, 20, 50)
- slot_size_gb: size of each slot (GB)
- pinned_share: fraction of slots that are allowed to be pinned at any time (0.0 - 1.0)
- effective_hit_rate: simulated overall KV hit-rate after slotization
- pref_overhead: multiplier for token cost due to prefetching/probing
- monthly_gpu_token_cost_savings: estimated $ saved on GPU token spend vs baseline, per month
- estimated_infra_delta: rough infra cost delta (more slots = fragmented memory, small ops cost), negative means extra cost
- net_monthly_savings: monthly_gpu_token_cost_savings + estimated_infra_delta - expected operational overhead (approx)

Scenario table (rows are stylized simulation outputs):

slots_total,slot_size_gb,pinned_share,effective_hit_rate,pref_overhead,monthly_gpu_token_cost_savings,estimated_infra_delta,net_monthly_savings,notes
10,50,0.5,0.235,1.08,$11,200,-$600,$10,000,"Improved heavy tenant hit-rate but cold-rotation cost high; infra fragmentation modest"
20,25,0.6,0.265,1.10,$15,800,-$1,200,$13,000,"Sweet spot for current traffic mix, good savings per 100k req/day"
50,10,0.4,0.240,1.18,$9,500,-$3,000,$6,000,"Lots of small slots -> more overhead and pref costs; hit-rate uplift modest"
100,5,0.7,0.278,1.22,$18,400,-$6,500,$11,000,"High slot count helps if pinned_share is high, but infra ops and probe costs grow"
5,100,0.2,0.205,1.05,$4,100,-$300,$3,500,"Very coarse slots — does not protect heavy tenants well"

Interpretation notes (working thoughts):
- There is a tradeoff: increasing slots_total sometimes increases effective_hit_rate (by protecting heavy tenants from eviction) but also raises the prefetch/probe overhead (pref_overhead). The net sweet spot depends on pinned_share and slot_size.
- In the simulated traffic mix, the 20-slot / 25GB slot configuration had strong ROI: moderate infra delta and highest net savings per month.

Back-of-envelope math used for savings column: (baseline token spend - scenario token spend) * monthly_tokens_per_unit_cost.
- Baseline monthly tokens (estimate): 1.4e9 tokens across requests. Baseline GPU token spend = 1.4e9 * $0.0000007 = $980. Scenario token spend derived from effective_hit_rate and pref_overhead.

Sensitivity checks I ran (notes):
- If heavy tenants are only 40% of requests (instead of 60%), slotized gains drop ~30% because fewer concentrated hot keys to protect.
- If cold-eviction penalty increases to 800 tokens (longer repop cost), net savings flip negative for high-slot churn configs.
- If token cost per token halves (model moves to cheaper infra or quantized ops), absolute $s fall and slotized ROI margin shrinks; still can make sense where latency SLOs are critical.

Operational considerations / open questions:
- How to implement pinning policy: static mapping of top-N customers to dedicated slots vs dynamic pin-on-hot-detection with TTL?
- Coordination overhead: need route-level instrumentation and a cheap lease mechanism to avoid two nodes pinning same slot concurrently.
- Migration path: start with pilot for 10 heavy tenants pinned on 8 slots (2 slots reserved) and telemetry to measure actual hit-rate improvements.
- How to dimension slot_size: should be measured in effective prefix footprint, not raw bytes. Likely compresses differently for different model families.

Recommended next steps (practical):
1) Run a small spike pilot: pick 8 heavy tenants (by qps) and allocate 2 slots each (10-slot pool). Collect 6 weeks of telemetry. (Owner: Marco)
2) Add simulation that samples real prefix cardinalities from production logs (not synthetic median). This will tighten effective_hit_rate estimates. (Owner: Elena)
3) Implement cheap pin-lease prototype in staging (lease TTL 30s, fallback to shared LRU) and run A/B with control group. (Owner: Tomáš)
4) Re-run cost model with actual infra amortization numbers (GPU amortization & SSD costs per GB) to replace rough estimated_infra_delta. (Owner: Finance-eng partner)

Quick TODOs (short):
- [ ] Pull real prefix cardinality histogram for top 200 tenants (queries: infra/metrics repo).
- [ ] Hook simulated slot model to trace-level sampling to validate cold-eviction token counts.
- [ ] Add latency impact column to future sheet (p99 delta) — users care about latency more than $s sometimes.

Notes to self: this doc should not be treated as final -- a lot of assumptions are placeholders. The aim is to pick an actionable pilot that is likely to show clear telemetry improvements without major infra refactor. Keep conservative on pinned_share for first pilot to avoid overcommitting memory.
